dedupe_keys.name: analyse von interdependenzen zwischen kritis inter 3 guide 2nd edition 2020

description: This German guide sets out a practical method for utilities and municipal authorities to analyse interdependencies between critical infrastructures across a whole supply area, so that cascading failures are considered in risk and crisis management. It covers why an interdependency analysis is needed, its three analytical steps of system analysis, complexity reduction and sensitivity analysis, how to carry it out in practice, and a set of standardised elements and relationships as a working basis, with an annex and references, drawing on the electricity, water supply, wastewater and food supply sectors. It was written by A. Dierich, U. Bösche and S. Wurbs of inter 3 in Berlin, 2nd updated edition February 2020 (ISBN 978-3-9819610-4-1), based on the BMBF-funded SIMKAS-3D, Safefresh and KIRMin research projects. The 40-page PDF is available as a free download; it is copyright inter 3, and no open licence is named. Caveats: it is in German, and the element lists reflect the German KRITIS context. It supports qualitative interdependency mapping as a first step before simulation; a related record is the Dutch socio-technical infrastructure interdependencies dataset.
